properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31: "how do we resolve the ophyd-service issue so that I can start implementing an alternate design?" Nothing chosen. He is BLOCKED on a real project, so this is a question about the cheapest unblock rather than about the right long-term shape.

═══ WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ═══
· A GIT WORKTREE GIVES THE DESIGN A BRANCH. The store is single-writer PER DIRECTORY, so a worktree is a separate directory and gets its own live graph. `reflow2-mcp --graph-path ./.reflow2/graph --import <export>` seeds it in one command; `--import` was confirmed present on the binary. This is documented in the `parallel-work` skill — framed for TWO PEOPLE, never for exploration, which is why nobody found it.
· `git switch` does NOT branch the design. One store for the repo and all its branches. That trap is recorded and has bitten before as four phantom drifts.
· CROSS-FORK COMPARISON WORKS. `analyze_alternatives` was run end-to-end on a real fork of this design: main 73 structural defects against fork 72, with node-level divergence reported, opening throwaway graphs and never touching the live one. Ophyd's claim that the health machinery is fork-blind is PARTLY WRONG and they should be told.
· WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT: cross-boundary edges, one session seeing both, and a one-call fork.

═══ 🛑 THE GAP THAT ACTUALLY BEARS ON HIS FEAR ═══
His stated worry is "reversals of previously settled requirements and accepted ideas". The schema already says a `lineage: derived` requirement is GOVERNED_BY the Decision that created it and "if the decision is re-opened the requirement may lose its reason to exist" — but lineage is 205/205 `original` (the default) and nothing reads it. So today NOTHING CAN TELL HIM WHICH REQUIREMENTS LOSE THEIR BASIS if the alternative reverses a decision. That is the one computation that would make the fork safe rather than merely possible.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
① FORK NOW, CLASSIFY NOTHING. Worktree + import, work in the fork, compare with analyze_alternatives, register_alternative to anchor it. ⭐ Unblocks him today with zero new machinery. ⚠️ The reversal set stays a judgement he holds in his head, which is the thing he said he was afraid of.
② FORK NOW, AND CLASSIFY ONLY THE BLAST RADIUS FIRST. Before forking, `propagate_from` the decisions the alternative would reverse, and set `lineage: derived` + GOVERNED_BY on the requirements in that radius that genuinely exist BECAUSE of those decisions. ⭐ Bounded — a handful of nodes, not 205 — and it produces the written list "these lose their basis if X reverses" that answers his fear directly. ⚠️ Classification is a judgement per node and a wrong one writes a false provenance claim; and it is retro-fitting, which is harder than doing it at capture.
③ BUILD WORLD-SCOPING FIRST. The ergonomics he actually wants. ⚠️ Blocks the project for as long as it takes, and `dec:parallel-alternatives` argues it bakes fork-awareness into every detector. Its own precondition — that branch-by-file teach what the scoping primitive must preserve — is unmet precisely because nobody has run a real fork yet.
④ FORK NOW AND TREAT IT AS THE EXPERIMENT. Take ① or ②, and record what the fork actually turns out to need. ⭐ This is the evidence `dec:parallel-alternatives` deferred world-scoping pending, and it costs nothing extra beyond noticing.

═══ ⚠️ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside rather than used to decide ═══
(1) ② risks the retro-classification trap: deciding after the fact why a requirement exists is exactly the reconstruction this project distrusts elsewhere, and `original` being the default means there is no record of which were ever considered.
(2) The worktree route has a real cost nobody has paid yet — the MCP config must point at the worktree's graph path, and getting that wrong means silently editing the wrong design. That failure mode is worse than the one being avoided.
(3) Nothing here has been tried on ophyd-service itself. Everything verified was verified on reflow2's own graph, which is a different shape and a different size.
properties.name: OPEN — what is the minimum path to start implementing ophyd-service's alternate design today, given the fork mechanism exists and the derived-requirement tier is unpopulated?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm discipline — ideas as ideas, nothing promoted, and the verifications kept separate from the options so a later reader can tell what was measured from what was proposed.

Kept as one node because it is one question with one deadline: he is blocked now. The long-term shape (whether world-scoping gets built) is a different question and lives on `fact:the-fork-ask-is-a-deferred-branch-whose-reopening-condition-is-now-met`; merging them would let the cheap unblock be held hostage to the expensive decision, which is how the project got parked in the first place.
